L2t: Passive movements are one of several types of joint movement used in physiotherapy and exercise, alongside active and active-assisted movements.
L3t: In passive movements an external force (a therapist or machine) moves the joint, so the person makes no muscular effort and nothing resists the motion.
L4t: Passive movements are movements done to a person without any resistance, which stop at the end of the available range rather than stretching beyond it.
L2f: Passive movements were first described in ancient Greek gymnastics and were mainly used to train athletes for competition.
L3f: In passive movements the therapist applies resistance throughout the motion and pushes the joint past its normal limit to gain extra range.
L4f: Passive movements are movements performed against resistance that stretch the joint at the end of its range.
cand_true: Movement without resistance, stopping at end of range
cand_wrong1: Movement with resistance, stretching at end of range
cand_wrong2: Movement performed by the person's own muscle contraction without help
